analysis.title: Navigating Japan's shifting cross-asset outlook (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: Nikkei 225 closed down 0.3% on Monday (2 Nov) after clawing back early losses. Last week the index traded across a 4.4-percentage point peak-to-trough range.
Under the surface, Kioxia fell 15.8% on Monday after a disappointing quarterly outlook. Tokyo Electron and Panasonic Holdings gained more than 5% on stronger earnings guidance.
USDJPY is holding around 158 as investors assess whether more hawkish BoJ language could prompt another unwind of yen-funded positions.
BoJ held its policy rate at 1.25% on 30 October. It said underlying inflation is broadly consistent with the 2% target and put more emphasis on upside price risks.

BoJ surprised by accelerating annual ETF sales to JPY 860bn (book value) from January 2027, 2.6x the prior JPY 330bn pace. UBS expects limited direct market impact: annual sales are about 0.1% of total market trading value, against JPY 7.2tr of corporate buybacks so far in 2026.

UBS now expects BoJ hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, earlier than its prior timetable, and keeps its 1.75% terminal rate forecast. Tokyo headline inflation rose to 2.8% in October and underlying inflation was 2.6%.

UBS sees yen downside capped by higher Japanese rates, which encourage domestic capital retention and lower hedging costs for overseas assets. A sustained yen rally is not yet supported: oil weighs on Japan's external balance, US yields are attractive, the US-Japan 2-year yield gap is 2.5-2.7 percentage points, and Japanese real rates are negative.

UBS keeps an Attractive view on Japanese equities and sees the volatility as a chance to add selectively. It favors resilient earnings, strong shareholder returns and structural growth, and warns against concentrated momentum and AI positions and against indiscriminate dip-buying in AI names.
UBS keeps its 12-month 10-year JGB yield forecast at about 2.9%, and USDJPY near 158 into March, June and September 2027.
US midterms on Tuesday (3 Nov): all 435 House seats, 35 of 100 Senate seats and 36 governorships. RCP average puts Trump net approval at -20pps and the Democratic generic-ballot lead at 8.9pps.

UBS midterm probabilities: 50% Democrats win both chambers, 40% Democrats win the House with Republicans holding the Senate, 10% Republicans hold both. It expects more oversight and harder fiscal talks but limited policy change, no derailing of data-center expansion, and possible debt-ceiling volatility in 2027. It does not treat the midterms as a binary market event.

Brent fell 8.3% to USD 104 on Monday and European natural gas fell more than 9% after the US and Iran signaled willingness to negotiate. The US 10-year yield fell 2bp. Attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz continue and no terms for reopening are agreed.

UBS stays moderately constructive on oil near term, seeing Brent near USD 110 at year-end and USD 90 by June 2027 as Hormuz traffic recovers. It cites low global inventories, largely complete strategic reserve releases and recovering Chinese imports. It sees broad commodity exposure as a portfolio resilience tool.

Selective exposure to quality names with resilient earnings momentum and demonstrated AI demand capture, not indiscriminate dip-buying.

Tokyo Electron and Panasonic Holdings issued stronger earnings guidance and rose more than 5% on Monday 2 Nov.
UBS says recent earnings dispersion in Japan reinforces the need for selectivity.

UBS terminal-rate forecast, unchanged, with hikes now expected in December 2026 and March 2027.
UBS expects USDJPY near current levels with two-way volatility.

risk_factors: Further yen carry unwind if BoJ language turns more hawkish.
Earnings dispersion and concentrated momentum and AI positioning in Japanese equities.
Oil path depends on US-Iran diplomacy, Gulf production and shipping reliability, and global demand.
Possible debt-ceiling negotiation volatility in 2027 after the midterms.
vol_and_positioning: Nikkei traded across a 4.4-percentage point peak-to-trough range last week, and the report describes Japanese equity volatility as elevated.
Investors are watching whether hawkish BoJ language triggers another unwind of yen carry (yen-funded) positions.
UBS expects continued two-way volatility across equities, rates and currencies.
geopolitical: US and Iran signaled willingness to negotiate over the conflict disrupting Middle Eastern energy supplies. Iran authorized its government to pursue talks and the US was reported ready to give diplomacy more time.
Attacks on vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue, and no terms for fully reopening the waterway are agreed.
US midterm elections on 3 November decide control of Congress.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS keeps Attractive on Japanese equities: fundamentals are supportive, ETF sales are small versus JPY 7.2tr of buybacks, and volatility creates entry points.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated volatility, a possible yen carry unwind on hawkish BoJ language, and wide earnings dispersion (Kioxia -15.8%) argue against concentrated momentum and AI exposure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another unwinding of yen-funded positions triggered by more hawkish BoJ language.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical market is tight: inventories are down sharply, strategic reserve releases are largely complete and Chinese imports are recovering, so UBS sees Brent near USD 110 at year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: US-Iran negotiations could remove part of the geopolitical risk premium, as Brent's 8.3% drop to USD 104 showed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Agreement on terms to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with traffic recovering faster than UBS's path to USD 90 by June 2027.

theme_stances.evidence: Yen downside capped, though a sharp rebound looks unlikely.
